label: PF Backlog 650
title: Gates: review-churn guard - disposition before re-review, bounded diff reviews per item

decisions.note: HIL requested the review-churn guard; design sha 6f45b030474f has 0 pending findings.

brief.problem: Review/fix/re-review loops are invisible; every commit changes the SHA and forces another review.
brief.why_now: EDP-10 required 8 diff reviews; discipline alone failed.
brief.success: Re-review is blocked until dispositions exist or a reasoned --rereview; completions over budget fail.

objective: Bound Gate 2.5 review churn with a disposition-before-re-review guard and a review-budget check, so re-reviews are deliberate and auditable.
acceptance_criteria: A single owner (scripts/dev/architect_review.py) exposes review_budget()/diff_reviews()/churn_verdict() from config/architect-review.json (warn_after=2, fail_after=4, scope=after_gate1); both run --mode diff and scripts/dev/review_churn_check.py consume those functions, with no duplicated thresholds/counting.

A diff re-review is refused when a prior diff review exists after the Gate 1 epoch and item.review_dispositions.diff is empty; --rereview requires a non-empty --reason, which is redacted, capped at 500 chars and stored as rereview_reason in the evidence.

review_churn_check.py counts only diff reviews at/after the latest Gate 1 decision (all if none), prints a deterministically sorted table and --json, warns when count >2 and fails a completion in the committed diff when count >4 unless the item has a HIL-attested review_churn decision (by hil:*, note >=40 chars citing the review sha); --report exits 0; an unreadable review dir/base ref exits 2 (fail closed).

Tests cover the boundary semantics (2/4 are pass, 3 warns, 5 fails), the Gate 1 epoch, the refusal and reasoned override, redaction/cap, the HIL-attested escape, --json/--report and the fail-closed git/evidence path; docs/REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE.md states one diff review per freeze, disposition-before-re-review and the budget.
approach: architect_review.py owns config-driven review_budget(), diff_reviews() and churn_verdict(); run --mode diff refuses an undispositioned re-review unless --rereview --reason (redacted/capped) and records rereview_reason. scripts/dev/review_churn_check.py imports those helpers, counts reviews after the Gate 1 epoch, prints a sorted table/--json, warns >2, fails >4 for completions unless a HIL-attested review_churn decision cites the review sha, and exits 2 on unreadable git/evidence. Add pytest coverage and the REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE budget section; register the check in the precheck gate list.

prior_decisions: Gate 2.5 evidence is bound to the exact diff SHA (BI-PF-1469/1470); every new commit invalidates prior evidence.
One review per item+SHA unless --rereview (architect_review.py run); dispositions are main-thread-owned and keyed by sig (BI-PF-1449).
BI-PF-1479 added the decision table + overall recommendation; the HIL can see dispositions beside findings.
EDP-10 (BI-PF-1302) required 8 diff reviews because fixes were made after each review instead of batching/dispositioning.
existing_path: scripts/dev/architect_review.py: _latest_review / run / _ingest; run refuses the same item+sha unless --rereview but does not guard a new SHA with undispositioned findings.
engineering/reviews/<item>-<sha>.json (mode design|diff) are committed evidence; item.review_dispositions[mode] holds dispositions.
precheck runs architect_review_check.py for the current SHA; it does not inspect review churn.
docs/REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE.md documents the gate order but not a review budget.
assumptions: A code freeze epoch is the latest Gate 1 decision; only diff reviews after it count (long-lived items are not permanent offenders).
The budget is strict-greater-than: count 2 pass, 3 warns, 4 pass, 5 fails; thresholds live in config/architect-review.json.
The review_churn escape is HIL-only (by hil:*), must cite the review sha and a >=40-char reason; self-service bypass is rejected.
review_churn_check resolves the base exactly like gate2_completion (--base or merge-base develop HEAD) and fails closed if git/evidence is unavailable.
rereview_reason and review_churn entries are append-only residue (rollback does not rewrite evidence).
divergences: Enforcement is in architect_review + precheck (not core.backlog.set_status) to avoid a write recursion.

impact_review.evidence: No HTTP surface: scripts/dev gate tooling + a pytest test.

evidence: architect_review.py run --mode diff refuses a new diff review for an item when a previous diff review exists and item.review_dispositions.diff is empty, unless --rereview is passed with a non-empty --reason; the reason is stored in the evidence JSON as rereview_reason.

scripts/dev/review_churn_check.py counts diff reviews per item, prints shas/dates and an advisory warning above 2, and fails a completion in the committed diff when an item has more than 4 diff reviews unless the item carries a review_churn decision (append-only ledger); --report is a non-blocking dry run.

Tests prove the refusal without dispositions, the --rereview+reason override, the warn/fail thresholds, the review_churn justification escape and the report mode; docs/REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE.md documents one diff review per code freeze + disposition-before-re-review; precheck passes.

impact_review.evidence: Python tooling (scripts/ + test-framework); no shipped product logic.
Extends architect_review.py as the single review owner; review_churn_check imports its budget/count/verdict helpers. No duplicate counting or thresholds.
--rereview remains; existing evidence/JSON is unchanged; only new completions over budget fail.
Review/precheck tooling only; append-only evidence; rollback is a revert and leaves reasoned rereview entries intentionally.

verification: pytest test_review_churn.py: 14 passed (boundaries 2/3/4/5, inclusive epoch, HIL attestation allowlist/hil_confirmed, corrupt evidence fail-closed, CLI --json/--report/exit codes, redaction/PEM/URL).
The review-churn gate runs in precheck fast for backlog changes; this item is its first live user (4 diff reviews -> warn, not fail).
risks: Legitimate iterative work is blocked: mitigated by the >4 budget, a review_churn decision, and --rereview with a reason.
Review files from other branches inflate the count: mitigated by counting only this item's committed evidence (the item's reviews are evidence, not branch-scoped) and a baseline/justification.
rollback: Revert the tooling commit; review evidence/JSON is unchanged.
evidence: Design pre-check (BI-PF-1480): answered 10 checklist item(s) before Gate 1.5

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=f744c6e324f1
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - Enforcement is duplicated: `architect_review.py` (refusal) and `review_churn_check.py` (warn/fail) each re-implement the "diff review for item X" counting and threshold semantics (>2, >4). Violates CL-001 single-writer; thresholds/logic must be single-sourced (e.g. `config/architect-review.json`) and consumed by both, with a stated owner.
  - The `review_churn` escape hatch is self-service: the design defines no attestation (who, why text validation, when it expires) for the append-only ledger entry, so the very actor the gate constrains can bypass it. Require structured justification + author + linkage to the failing findings.
  - Counting baseline is undefined. The guard counts all-time diff reviews while the docs promise "one diff review per code freeze"; without an explicit freeze-scoped baseline/epoch, long-lived items permanently exceed the budget and need a ledger entry every cycle. Risks mention a baseline but no mechanism or invariant is stated.
  - "Fails a completion in the committed diff" has no defined comparison semantics (base ref, shallow clone, no-HEAD runs). Non-deterministic precheck results; specify the ref resolution and test it (guardrail 5/6).
  - `--reason` free text is persisted verbatim into committed evidence JSON with no redaction/retention rule; risk of secrets/PII entering the repo (guardrail 9).
  - Threshold constants (2/4) appear hardcoded in two places with no config, and strict-greater-than vs greater-or-equal is not pinned by the design; tests must lock the exact boundary semantics.
MINOR:
  - Read-then-write guard has a TOCTOU race between the refusal check and evidence write; acceptable for single-user tooling but should be documented as an accepted limitation.
  - Observability is a stdout table only; no machine-readable (`--json`) output, exit-code taxonomy, or counter emitted for churn trending — hurts long-term diagnosis (guardrail 10).
  - Behaviour when review evidence is absent/partial in the checkout (fresh clone, partial fetch) is unspecified; define the fail-open vs fail-closed choice explicitly.
  - Rollback leaves already-written `rereview_reason` / `review_churn` entries in evidence; confirm this is intentional append-only residue and state it in the rollback note.
NIT:
  - Register `review_churn_check` in the existing precheck gate registry rather than adding a parallel invocation path, to keep gate ordering and reporting uniform.
  - Sort the churn table deterministically (item, then date, then sha) so golden-output tests and human diffs stay stable.
SUMMARY:
  - Design direction is sound (disposition-before-re-review + budget gate) and stays within the tooling-Python language rule, but the gate is currently advisory in practice: duplicated counting logic in two scripts, a self-service bypass, and an undefined counting baseline (all-time vs per-freeze) undermine the invariant it claims to enforce.
  - Top risks before Gate 1.5: single-source the thresholds/counting, define the freeze-scoped baseline and git-ref semantics, and require attested `review_churn` entries; otherwise the "one diff review per code freeze" promise is not verifiable and legitimate long-lived items degrade into permanent blocked states.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=6f45b030474f
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - HIL escape is self-service: "by hil:*, note >=40 chars citing the review sha" is a string-format check with no actor allowlist or signature; any author can mint `hil:<self>` and a 40-char note containing the sha to bypass the >4 fail. Define authorized attesters (or require the attestation to land via the main-thread/disposition path, CL-002) and test rejection of a self-minted attestation.
  - Gate 1 epoch derivation is underspecified: "latest Gate 1 decision" has no stated ordering invariant (commit order vs. author timestamp vs. file mtime) and no handling of rebases/cherry-picks that rewrite Gate 1 commits. State and test the invariant (e.g., by commit SHA reachability from HEAD), or the count is nondeterministic across clones.
  - Count scope is not tied to the committed evidence set: counting "reviews not branch-scoped" means untracked, stashed, or foreign-branch review files on a developer machine can push a clean item over 4 (or shield it if removed locally before CI). Count only review files present in the base ref / the item's committed evidence and assert the local-vs-CI count match in a test.
  - "Diff review" identity is undefined: how does churn_check map the diff under review to one item's evidence dir and decide which files are "diff reviews" vs. earlier-mode reviews? Without a filename/manifest contract, the count is heuristic; specify the evidence manifest format and test mixed-mode evidence.
  - Refusal semantics have a trivial bypass: `--rereview --reason` accepts any non-empty string; nothing binds the reason to the prior review (e.g., cite prior sha / disposition gap). Require the reason to reference the superseded review sha (mirroring the churn attestation rule) and test that a generic reason is rejected.
  - Fail-closed exit 2 on missing base ref will false-positive in shallow CI clones (fetch-depth=1, detached refs). Define the fetch depth/ref-resolution precondition in the design and test a shallow-clone scenario, otherwise the precheck becomes flaky infrastructure rather than a guardrail.
  - Redaction contract is unspecified (item 9/retention): "redacted" has no stated pattern set, order-of-operations vs. the 500-char cap (truncation can split a secret or drop the redaction marker), or retention/expiry for `rereview_reason` stored in evidence. Define the redactor, cap-after-redact, and a retention note; test a reason containing a token-like string.
MINOR:
  - `churn_verdict` return shape (count/warn/fail + reason codes) is not pinned; consumers (`run --mode diff`, churn_check, precheck) could re-derive booleans, re-creating the duplication this ticket exists to remove. Define and test the verdict contract and assert precheck consumes it rather than re-implementing exit-code mapping.
  - Warning vs. failure signaling is print-only; no stable event/metric hook (guardrail 10). Even a single structured log event (`review_churn_warn|fail`, item, count) would keep the gate diagnosable when it blocks a merge at 02:00.
  - `--report` exiting 0 regardless of verdict conflates "ran successfully" with "no findings"; consumers can't distinguish a pass from a scan error. Exit 0 with verdict in JSON is fine, but state it explicitly in docs and test both a warn-level and fail-level `--report` run.
  - Rollback story ignores persisted evidence: reverting the tooling commit leaves `rereview_reason` fields and any HIL churn attestations in evidence files; downstream readers of evidence JSON need a tolerance rule for unknown fields (test forward/backward compat).
  - The "warn_after=2, fail_after=4" semantics ("2/4 pass, 3 warns, 5 fails") are boundary-tested but the config loader isn't shown validating `0 <= warn_after < fail_after`; a bad config silently inverts the gate. Add a config-validation test.
NIT:
  - Cap-before-redact ordering should be documented as redact-then-cap so a 500-char boundary cannot clip mid-marker.
  - Sorted-table key should be explicitly "review file path, then sha" so the fixture tests don't depend on dict iteration order.
  - The recurring [MINOR] about `_render_review`/`_item_dispositions` path coverage applies analogously here: the churn table renderer (missing-item/unknown-status rows) deserves a direct unit test, not just the round-trip test.
SUMMARY:
  - none
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=7aed4fdd42cd
BLOCKER:
  - AC requires an unreadable base ref to exit 2 fail-closed; `review_churn_check.py` returns 0 with `skipped`/`base_unavailable` (and the new doc legitimizes it), so the gate silently no-ops whenever `merge-base develop` is unavailable — fail-open.
  - No tests at all exercise `review_churn_check.py` CLI behavior (`--json`, `--report`, exit codes, fail-closed git/evidence path), all explicitly required by the AC.
MAJOR:
  - Rows are printed in `g2.transitions(base)` order with no sort; the AC mandates a deterministically sorted table, so output ordering is an unstated dependency on ledger/git traversal order.
  - `base = a.base or ar._git_text([...])` runs outside the `try`; if `_git_text` raises on a missing ref the process dies with an uncaught traceback (exit 1) instead of the specified exit 2.
  - With the default path yielding `skipped` → exit 0, and `--report` also exit 0, there is no reachable local configuration where the churn budget ever fails — the gate only works when `--base`/full history is passed, but nothing enforces that.
  - `--reason` supplied without `--rereview` is silently ignored (guard returns early), so an operator gets no feedback that their rationale was discarded.
MINOR:
  - `evaluate()` calls `ar._get_item` per item with no per-row error isolation; one malformed/missing item aborts the whole scan (exit 2) instead of surfacing as a row-level failure.
  - `attesters` allowlist is a single hardcoded principal (`hil:srinikc`) baked into a committed config — no environment/rotation story, and an org-wide escape hatch tied to one account.
  - `review_guard` recomputes `churn_verdict` (git ls-tree + item read) inside `main` which then separately recomputes `diff_sha`/`_get_item` — duplicated I/O on the hot review path.
  - Redaction regex only covers `key/token/secret/password/authorization` and `bearer`; URLs with embedded credentials or PEM blocks in a reason are stored unredacted.
NIT:
  - Unrelated reflow of `blocking_findings`/`skip_globs` arrays adds pure diff noise to an otherwise scoped change.
  - The `review_budget.note` in config restates `2`/`4` as literals, a textual duplication of the thresholds the AC says must have one owner.
  - `getattr(a, "reason", "")` is defensive noise — the parser always defines `--reason`.
  - Doc line "Reviews are counted from committed `HEAD` evidence; a missing base ref reports `skipped`" documents the fail-open behavior as intended, locking in the blocker above.
SUMMARY:
  - The single-owner budget/diff-review/churn-verdict layering and reuse of `g2.transitions` are the right shape, and boundary/epoch/attestation/redaction tests are solid.
  - However the gate's fail-closed contract is inverted for the default base-ref path, CLI-level tests required by the AC are entirely absent, and output ordering is not deterministic — these must land before this can be trusted as a Gate 2.5 control.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=fd5330e4b7a2
BLOCKER:
  - `diff_reviews()` fails open, not closed: missing/renamed `engineering/reviews` yields empty `ls-tree`/glob (no error) and corrupt/unreadable JSON is swallowed by `except Exception: continue`, so churn count silently drops to 0 and the gate passes. AC requires an unreadable review dir to exit 2.
  - Gate verdict mixes snapshots: reviews are read from committed HEAD (`committed=True`) while `review_epoch`/`churn_attested` read the item from the working tree via `_get_item`. An uncommitted `review_churn` attestation (or Gate 1 decision) flips a committed-diff failure to pass — an integrity/attestation bypass.
MAJOR:
  - `redact_reason` is regex heuristics on text that gets committed to git: unlabeled secrets (`ghp_...`, AWS keys, `pwd=`, `X-Api-Key:`, bare tokens) pass through unredacted into permanent evidence. Redaction alone is not sufficient for a committed audit artifact; consider storing a hash/short prefix instead.
  - Same-sha re-review overwrites `{item}-{sha}.json`, so repeat reviews of one freeze's diff are never counted — the "one diff review per freeze" budget undercounts exactly the behavior it targets (pre-existing write path, but this feature makes it load-bearing).
  - `precheck.py` hard-wires `review-churn` as a fast gate with no `--base` override: on any checkout without a local `develop` ref (main-based branches, shallow CI clones) every precheck fails closed with exit 2. Needs a configurable base or graceful degrade.
  - Attestation allowlist is a single hardcoded principal (`hil:srinikc`) in config with no pattern support (`hil:*` implied by AC) — key-person, non-rotatable, and a config edit silently widens the escape hatch with no schema/validation or audit event.
MINOR:
  - Tests never exercise the AC-required "unreadable evidence path exits 2"; only git/base-ref errors are covered, because the code path in question cannot currently fail.
  - `review_churn_check.evaluate()` reaches into `ar._get_item` and `rc.g2` privates across modules; `churn_verdict` returns redundant `fail`/`allowed` fields — thin public API contract for a "single owner".
  - Refusal is bypassed entirely once any `review_dispositions.diff` exists, so unlimited reasoned re-reviews remain possible pre-completion; only the completion gate bounds churn — docs should say the budget is soft in-flight.
  - Unparsable review `at` timestamps default to "counted" while unparsable Gate 1 `at` yields an empty epoch that counts everything — behavior is fail-closed but undocumented and untested.
NIT:
  - Unrelated reformatting of `blocking_findings`/`skip_globs` arrays in `config/architect-review.json` adds diff noise to an audit-sensitive config.
  - Missing blank line between `test_bad_budget_config_fails_closed` and `test_reason_flag_requires_rereview` (PEP8 E305); `--json` mode still emits human warn/fail events to stderr.
  - Docs mention `--base` escape for missing `develop` but the precheck wiring provides no way to pass it.
SUMMARY:
  - Sound architecture on the surface: single owner (`architect_review.py`) with config-driven budget, deterministic table/`--json`, and boundary tests at 2/3/4/5 match the AC.
  - However the gate is not the fail-closed control the AC requires: unreadable/missing evidence silently passes, and the verdict composes committed reviews with working-tree item state, letting an uncommitted HIL attestation suppress a hard failure.
  - Top risks: fail-open evidence handling (BLOCKER), committed-artifact secret leakage via weak redaction (MAJOR), and precheck coupling to a local `develop` ref (MAJOR).
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=92f2a86a5671
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - `_ingest` renames an existing review to `{sha}-prev-<ms>.json` and writes a new one; `diff_reviews()` globs `{item_id}-*.json` and both files carry `"mode": "diff"`, so a single re-review permanently inflates the churn count (and creates unprompted evidence files that other gates may also pick up). Untested and self-defeating for the budget.
  - Redaction is regex-heuristic only (`redact_reason`); novel secret formats (e.g. `sk-...`, JWTs, bare passwords in prose) pass through into committed evidence. Combined with `--reason` free-text from operators, this is a weak guarantee for "redacted" as an acceptance promise — needs an explicit allowlist/post-hoc secret scan or a documented limitation.
  - `_after_epoch` uses strict `at > epoch`, but the acceptance criterion and the new doc say "at/after the Gate 1 epoch"; a review stamped exactly at the decision time is silently excluded, so boundary semantics differ from the stated contract (and no test pins this).
  - `review_churn_check.py` imports and calls `ar._git_text` (a module-private helper) for base-ref resolution; this cross-module coupling to a private symbol will break silently on refactor and bypasses any logging/observability that `_git_text` might later add.
  - Tests never exercise the `--rereview` main() flow end-to-end (refusal → override → `_ingest` prev-rename → `rereview_reason` persisted), which is precisely where the count-inflation bug lives; the acceptance criterion's "reasoned override ... stored as rereview_reason in the evidence" is only covered at function level.
MINOR:
  - `reason_flag_error` / `review_guard` are gated on `a.mode == "diff"` only; `--reason` with design mode is silently ignored instead of erroring, inconsistent with the "--reason requires --rereview" symmetry.
  - Citation check (`latest_sha in reason`) runs on the raw reason, but the stored/capped (500-char) copy may truncate the sha citation — evidence can lose the very reference that authorized the override; also `rereview_reason_sha256` hashes the post-redaction string, so it does not attest the operator's original input.
  - `redact_reason()` calls `review_budget()` (config read + validation) on every invocation, including per-row usage paths — small but avoidable I/O and a hidden dependency on config validity in a pure string function.
  - `diff_reviews(committed=True)` does `git show HEAD:<rel>` per evidence file (N+1 subprocesses); on repos with many reviews this is a measurable precheck latency cost — consider `cat-file --batch` or a single `git grep`.
  - `--report` docstring says "always exit 0" but scan errors still return 2; fine per fail-closed intent, yet the docstring and the doc line "--report exits 0" should state the exception to avoid operator confusion.
  - `evaluate()` synthesizes `warn_after: 0, fail_after: 0` for error rows; harmless because errors force exit 2, but the fabricated budget values leak into `--json` output and could mislead downstream consumers.
NIT:
  - Reformatting of unrelated config keys (`blocking_findings`, `skip_globs`) to multi-line inflates the diff and churns a file the churn gate itself watches — keep formatting-only changes out of behavioral PRs.
  - Table header prints "diff reviews after the Gate 1 epoch" even when `scope` is configured to something other than `after_gate1`; header should derive from the active scope.
  - Missing blank line before `def test_reason_flag_requires_rereview` (PEP8 E302-adjacent) in the new test file.
SUMMARY:
  - Solid single-owner design: `review_budget()/diff_reviews()/churn_verdict()` are genuinely consumed by both the run path and the new gate, thresholds live only in config, and fail-closed handling plus tests cover the 2/3/4/5 boundaries, epoch, attestation, and exit codes.
  - Top risks: the `-prev-` rename silently double-counts reviews (corrupting the very metric this feature enforces, and untested), regex-only redaction provides a weaker-than-stated secret guarantee, and the strict `>` epoch comparison diverges from the documented "at/after" semantics.
  - Recommend fixing the double-count and adding an end-to-end `--rereview` test before merge; the rest is hardening and observability polish.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

Gate 2.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=3ca3570efee5
BLOCKER:
  - none
MAJOR:
  - `diff_reviews(committed=True)` treats an empty `ls-tree` as "unreadable or empty" and raises; a branch with no committed reviews (a legitimate state) is indistinguishable from a git failure and hard-exits 2, making the gate fail-always rather than fail-closed.
  - Attestation fails open when evidence has no/empty `sha`: `latest = max(...)["sha"]` can be `""`, and `churn_attested` skips the citation check via `if latest_sha and ...`, so an over-budget item is allowed by an attestation that cites nothing.
  - precheck groups `review-churn` under "backlog" while its sibling Gate 2.5 gate `architect-review` is "quality"; if group determines which precheck runs where, the churn budget may not run on the path that enforces Gate 2.5/completion.
  - `redact_reason` has no generic secret patterns (`sk-…`, private-key-less high-entropy tokens, `--token <val>` form); the redacted-but-partial reason is persisted into `engineering/reviews` evidence that is committed to git — secret residue can ship.
  - Re-review archive (`-prev-<ms>.json`) makes one physical review count as two evidence rows for the same sha, inflating churn counts and triggering the warn budget on a legitimate, reasoned re-review (enshrined by `test_archived_rereview_counts_as_a_run` but contradicting "one diff review per freeze" counting integrity).
MINOR:
  - `--json` combined with `--report` writes a non-JSON `REPORT` line to stdout after the JSON document; and scan errors in `--json` mode emit no structured output at all, breaking machine consumers.
  - `review_guard` returns the redacted reason but `main` discards it and re-redacts the raw input; if the cited sha falls past the 500-char cap the stored `rereview_reason` omits the very sha it was validated against.
  - `--reason` without `--rereview` is only rejected in diff mode (`reason_flag_error` inside `if a.mode == "diff"`); design-mode `--rereview --reason` silently stores `rereview_reason` with no validation.
  - The committed git path (`ls-tree`/`show` in `diff_reviews` and `_item_committed`) has zero test coverage — fail-closed tests only exercise the working-tree corrupt-file path.
  - Threshold defaults `2`/`4` are duplicated as code fallbacks in `review_budget()` and hardcoded again in `docs/REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE.md` prose, risking drift from `config/architect-review.json`.
  - `redact_reason` is invoked twice per run (guard + main) with different inputs/outputs discarded, an avoidable divergence point for future edits.
NIT:
  - Unrelated reformat of `blocking_findings`/`skip_globs` in `architect-review.json` adds config churn orthogonal to BI-PF-1480.
  - `churn_verdict` computes `allowed = not (over and not attested)` alongside `fail = over and not attested`; one expression should derive from the other.
  - Docs line renders an ASCII `-` where an arrow/em-dash is intended, and the pre-existing binding-order line uses `?` placeholders.
SUMMARY:
  - Solid single-owner design: thresholds, epoch, counting and attestation are correctly centralized in `architect_review.py` and consumed by both entry points, with boundary/HIL/fail-closed tests largely present.
  - Top risks: fail-always (not fail-closed) on an empty committed review tree, fail-open attestation when `sha` is empty, possible churn-count inflation from `-prev-` archives, and incomplete secret redaction before evidence is committed.
  - Secondary: precheck group placement may silently skip the gate, machine output purity under `--json --report`, and the untested committed-git read path.
